# Independent audit: stochastic cubic and every triangle incidence

Audited in full:

* `candidate 6b3596acb8604c8b`
* `candidate 2a708bf626836967`

**Result: PASS. No correction required.** The theorem applies to every
interior source and balanced spanning three-normal circuit on an ordinary
triangle. It does not extend by itself to quadrilaterals or mixed fibers.

## Positive weighted maximizers

The row square F=max_j Q_j is nonnegative and at most the square of its
largest entry, including all zeros. At a fully positive row, each tied
maximizing smooth square-root branch is positive. Replacing the maximum
by such a branch gives a smooth function bounded above by the objective,
with equality at the putative local maximizer; it really does inherit a
local maximum. Thus the common transfer-gradient argument remains valid
at a tied maximum, and the nonzero branch-gradient difference excludes
that tie.

For two fully positive rows with unique maxima, the common weighted
gradient has all coordinates strictly positive. The proposed transfer
vectors annihilate it in both rows. Direct substitution gives Q_j(v)>0
in the equal-index case and Q_j(v)=Q_k(v)=1 in the different-index case.
The second derivative is Q_j(v)/sqrt(Q_j), not twice this value; the
source uses the correct coefficient. Its strict positivity contradicts
the local maximum for either sign of a sufficiently small transfer.
Unchanged zero rows require no differentiability.

## Two-zero-row boundary calculation

The same-column identity and both AM--GM comparisons hold even with
additional zeros. In the different-column case I independently expanded
all three displayed differences Z-Q_j and the determinant identity

    (1-z-La)(1-z-Lc)-L^2 acz
       =(1-z)[(1-aL)(1-cL)-z].

All agree exactly. The diagonal estimate uses a,c,L in [0,1], and the
L=0 branch is separately handled. Thus the boundary lemma has no hidden
positivity or denominator assumption.

## Compact extremum and Perron reduction

The stochastic polytope is compact, F and the spectral objective are
continuous, and a maximum exists. A violating maximum must have at least
two nonzero edges, so its three-node graph is connected. The absolute-value
Rayleigh argument and zero propagation give a strictly positive eigenvector.
Holding this vector fixed supplies strictly positive coefficients for a
weighted row maximum. It is a genuine global maximum of that weighted
functional because its Rayleigh quotient is bounded above by the global
spectral maximum at every matrix. The preceding reduction therefore
forces two zero rows, and the boundary lemma excludes the violation.

## Exact row minimization

The uniform-triangle sublevel formulas yield the minimizer
c*=x+y-xy/z in the upper interval when the row has distinct entries.
I independently checked G(c*)=c*/z algebraically. The lower-interval
ratio is decreasing when x>0 and constant when x=0. Every tied or zero
case is covered explicitly. In particular the zero row has infimum zero,
and (0,0,z) reaches it only as the positive threshold tends to zero;
the proof does not claim an attained minimizer there.

## Actual triangle transfer

The divergence identity has the correct sign: the cut's outward normal
is -v_i/||v_i||, and its flux for x-P_j is +t_ij sigma_i. The opposite
edge contributes 2k times its captured length fraction. Consequently
R_ij=Q_i-t_ij S_i/2 exactly. The entries X_ij=R_ij/(S_i M) are
nonnegative and their columns sum to one by sum_i v_i=0.

The actual cap is the lower sublevel X_i dot Xi<=a_i. Its threshold is
positive and interior to its projection interval, since the source is
interior and the normal is nonzero. The coarea derivative is
G_i'(a_i)=2M S_i, including a vertex-level cut because section length is
continuous at an interior level. Thus a_i G_i'(a_i)=2Q_i. The tangent
of sqrt(G_i) passes through zero and supports its concave profile on
the whole relevant projection interval; the constant continuation beyond
the upper endpoint is concave as used. Thresholds below the projection
minimum have G=0 and are omitted from the infimum. The row-minimum identity
therefore gives f_i=2phi(X_i) without a limiting interchange.

All cap boundaries have zero planar area, while edge fractions retain
their correct closed-cut values. An interior cutting line cannot coincide
with a triangle edge. No vertex-incidence case is discarded.

## Consequence for the spectral reduction

The independently audited spectral-objective reduction yields a triangle
or quadrilateral witness to any ordinary planar cubic failure. The present
all-incidence triangle theorem now excludes every triangular witness,
without a cap ceiling. Therefore any failure has an actual quadrilateral
witness with the same six sector areas and at least the same spectral
objective. This is a reduction, not a proof of the remaining quadrilateral
inequality.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
